name: Learn: Canary Deployments
objective: CKAD › Application Deployment. Run a new version alongside the stable one behind ONE Service and split traffic by replica ratio (label-based canary), then diagnose a canary that gets no traffic. Graded exactly.
description: Build a label-based canary: stable + canary Deployments sharing an app label, one Service fronting both, verify the split, and fix a canary that's excluded by a too-specific selector.

questions.title: Deploy the stable version
questions.teach:
A **canary** release runs the new version beside the stable one and gives it a slice of traffic. Both Deployments share a label (`app=web`) that one Service selects, so traffic splits by **replica ratio**. Start with stable.

**Gotcha:** each Deployment's own `selector` must include a distinguishing label (`track`) so it manages only *its* pods, not the other's.
questions.prompt:
In `canary-learn`, create Deployment `web-stable`: image `nginx:1.25`, **3** replicas, pod labels `app=web` AND `track=stable`, with its selector matching **both** labels.

Target: `web-stable` — nginx:1.25, 3 replicas, pod labels + selector `app=web`/`track=stable`.
questions.hint: Selector `matchLabels: {app: web, track: stable}`; pod template labels the same. 3 replicas.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: web-stable, namespace: canary-learn }
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: web, track: stable } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: web, track: stable } }
    spec:
      containers: [ { name: web, image: nginx:1.25 } ]
YAML

questions.title: Deploy the canary version
questions.teach:
Add the canary Deployment: new image, the **same** `app=web` label (so the Service picks it up) plus `track=canary`. With 3 stable : 1 canary replicas, the canary gets ~25% of traffic.

**Gotcha:** the shared `app=web` label is what puts canary pods behind the Service; `track` keeps the two Deployments separate.
questions.prompt:
In `canary-learn`, create Deployment `web-canary`: image `nginx:1.26`, **1** replica, pod labels `app=web` AND `track=canary`, selector matching both.

Target: `web-canary` — nginx:1.26, 1 replica, pod labels + selector `app=web`/`track=canary`.
questions.hint: Same shape as web-stable but `track: canary`, image `nginx:1.26`, 1 replica.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: web-canary, namespace: canary-learn }
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: web, track: canary } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: web, track: canary } }
    spec:
      containers: [ { name: web, image: nginx:1.26 } ]
YAML

questions.title: One Service fronting both
questions.teach:
One **Service** fronts both Deployments by selecting only the **shared** label (`app=web`) — NOT `track`. It load-balances across every matching ready pod, so the replica ratio becomes the traffic ratio.

**Gotcha:** if the Service selector includes `track`, it fronts only one version and the other gets no traffic.
questions.prompt:
Create a ClusterIP Service `web` in `canary-learn` (port 80 → targetPort 80) selecting **only** `app=web` (no `track`), so it fronts both stable and canary.

Target: Service `web` ClusterIP, port 80→80, selector is exactly `app=web`.
questions.hint: `spec.selector: {app: web}` — just the shared label, no track.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: { name: web, namespace: canary-learn }
spec:
  selector: { app: web }
  ports: [ { port: 80, targetPort: 80 } ]
YAML

verification.description: Service web: ClusterIP 80->80, selector exactly app=web

questions.title: Verify the traffic split
questions.teach:
The split is just the **endpoint ratio**: 3 stable + 1 canary ready pods = 4 endpoints, ~25% to the canary. Scale either Deployment to shift the split; scale canary up (and stable down) to **promote**, or delete the canary to roll back.

**Gotcha:** only **ready** pods become endpoints — a failing canary silently gets 0% traffic.
questions.prompt:
Confirm the canary is live: the `web` Service's endpoints must include pods from **both** Deployments — at least 3 from `web-stable` and at least 1 from `web-canary`.

Target: `web`'s endpoints include ≥3 web-stable pods AND ≥1 web-canary pod.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n canary-learn get endpoints web -o wide` — you should see 4 addresses. Make sure both Deployments' pods are Ready.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n canary-learn get endpoints web -o wide
kubectl -n canary-learn get pods -l app=web -L track

verification.description: web endpoints span both tracks (>=3 stable, >=1 canary)

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: canary gets no traffic
questions.teach:
A canary getting **no** traffic usually means the Service selector is **too specific** — it includes `track=stable`, so canary pods aren't selected. Loosen it to the shared label only.

**Gotcha:** patching `selector:{app:pay}` *merges* — `track` stays; you must set `track: null` (or `kubectl edit`) to actually remove the key.
questions.prompt:
Service `pay` in `canary-learn` fronts only its stable pods — `pay-canary` gets no traffic. Diagnose why and fix it so **both** are served. Don't delete it.

Target: `pay`'s endpoints include `pay-canary` pods.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n canary-learn get svc pay -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'` → it has `track: stable`. Remove that: `kubectl -n canary-learn patch svc pay -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"pay","track":null}}}'` (or edit to `selector: {app: pay}`).
questions.solution:
# patching selector:{app:pay} MERGES — track:stable would remain; set track:null to remove it
kubectl -n canary-learn patch svc pay -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"pay","track":null}}}'
kubectl -n canary-learn get endpoints pay -o wide

verification.description: pay endpoints now include pay-canary pods (selector loosened)
